summary: Multi-tenant 5xx wave following automated prefetch + cache sweep
customer_company: Polylingo Inc. (sampled) and other self-serve tenants
description:
Issue summary:
Automated prefetch/cache-sweep job ran across a subset of shard groups starting ~2026-03-10T12:05Z which coincided with a sharp rise in 5xx responses at the API gateway and upstream runtime process crashes. The event produced a multi-tenant error wave affecting self-serve customers and transiently raising our 5xx rate by ~8x for ~30 minutes.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: increased 5xx for text generation and streaming endpoints across us-east and spillover into us-west. Several customers (Polylingo Inc. observed) reported degraded performance and timeouts.
- Platform: serving-runtime processes on 4 shard groups experienced rapid restarts and elevated OOM/page-fault counts during the sweep window. API gateway returned 502/503 at scale due to upstream unavailability.

Environment:
- prod - us-east primary; partial spill to us-west during fallback routing.
- Autoscaler observed rapid scale-down attempts before the wave.

Steps to reproduce (observed sequence):
1) Prefetch/cache-sweep triggered by scheduled invalidation job (internal cron) at 2026-03-10T12:05Z across shard groups A,C,F.
2) Prefetch triggered high concurrency model loads and KV cache invalidations; runtime memory usage spiked and GC pressure increased.
3) Upstream runtimes began to OOM/restart; health-check flaps removed endpoints from the pool.
4) API gateway load redistributed, causing connection churn and 502/503 return for in-flight requests.
5) Autoscaler oscillation and prefetch retries amplified load, creating a retry storm.

Observed logs & metrics pointers:
- Dashboard (errors): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/metrics/5xx-spike?from=2026-03-10T11:50Z&to=2026-03-10T13:30Z
- Runtime shard crash trace: https://sentry.redwood.ai/issue/RT-78321
- Prefetch job history: internal-jobstore/prefetch/2026-03-10-12:05

Temporary impact mitigation in-flight:
- Disabled the scheduled full-sweep invalidation job at 2026-03-10T12:18Z (SRE action).
- Applied a soft concurrency cap to prefetch workers for affected shard groups at 2026-03-10T12:25Z.
- Scoped rolling restarts of runtimes for shards with persistent OOMs starting 12:30Z.

Requested from customer (Polylingo Inc.):
- Status updates and ETA for full service recovery. They reported 12 failed request traces and requested a root-cause follow-up.

Note: This ticket captures the operational incident and customer-facing support interactions. Follow-up work will be tracked in a separate postmortem/ops task once root cause confirmed.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Prefetch + cache invalidation created concurrent eager model loads exceeding expected memory headroom for some shards.
Sentry traces show repeated 'cudaMalloc' failure patterns immediately before runtime restarts (RT-78321).
Autoscaler logs indicate scale-down/scale-up oscillation between 12:10Z-12:35Z that likely exacerbated connection churn.
Kernel-selection logs: some big-model loads fell back to non-optimized kernels for long sequences, increasing memory usage (see runtime/pull/3721).
We were not rate-limiting prefetch across tenants; a global sweep created simultaneous hotloads across multiple tenants.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: scheduled sweep disabled and prefetch concurrency capped; targeted rolling restarts removed unhealthy runtimes; temporary global rate-limit for prefetch jobs enforced.
Next steps: implement tenant-aware prefetch throttling, add memory budget checks before eager model load, update cache-invalidation runbook to avoid full-shard simultaneous sweeps, and schedule a full postmortem (INC-20260310-001). Planned PRs for kernel logging and prefetch limiter: runtime/pull/3721, apigateway/pull/1189.
notes_for_postmortem: Quantify memory delta during sweep vs baseline per shard.
Run chaos test of prefetch sweeping with synthetic tenants to validate limiter behavior.
Add guard rails in autoscaler to avoid oscillation during high transient memory pressure.
